sentences.text: 4. Ld.
Counsel for revisionists reiterated the aforesaid grounds while making arguments before this Court.
It is stated that Ld. Trial Court passed impugned order without considering the material on record and applicable law.
He pleaded this Court to set aside the impugned order and discharge the revisionists.
5. Submissions heard.
Record perused.
6. All the contentions raised in the present revision petition by Ld. Counsel have been carefully considered by this Court vis-a-vis the various allegations in the complaint dated 07.10.2015.

In the opinion of this Court, all such contentions like contradictions in the statement/complaint of complainant; no specific details of entrustment of dowry articles; that allegations in complaint dated 07.10.2015 are false or fabricated; that there was no demand of dowry at any point of time; that no recovery was effected from or at the instance of accused/revisionists; that there is no material to directly or indirectly connect revisionists with the alleged charge; & that revisionist Varun and his wife Kamlesh were staying away, are either in the form of defence of the revisionists against the case of prosecution or mere bald averments.
All such claims and contentions may be appreciated only during trial, and cannot have any bearing on the nature of charge to be framed by Ld. Trial Court.
7. Ld. Trial Court in its order dated 22.06.2023 has categorically recorded all the allegations against the revisionists individually.

Further, a bare perusal of the complaint dated Pradeep Kumar & Anr.
vs. State of Delhi (NCT of Delhi) & Ram Kishore & Anr. vs. State of Delhi (NCT of Delhi) 07.10.2015 would provide that complainant has furnished all the necessary details of nature of dowry allegedly demanded, the nature of harassment allegedly meted out to her, the allegations of non return of her jewellery articles, the dates of different incidents and the alleged role of each of the family member including the husband namely Pradeep Kumar.
